newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pakistan would ask for rescheduling of its debt for three years if Islamabad fails to strike a deal with the International Monetary Fund for $1.5 billion medium-term enhanced structural adjustment facility loan.
- The government is considering a time schedule to privatise Pakistan State Oil, Pakistan Steel and Pakistan International Airlines.
- Trade policy for 1997/98 (July-June) is expected to be announced Tuesday.

- A sizable number of Pakistan Railways employees may face dismissal before the privatisation process kicks off as the private sector may not be willing to accept the huge liability of staff when it takes over the organisation.
- Pakistan indicated on Sunday that its efforts to broker peace talks between warring factions in bordering Afghanistan were succeeding.
- Five armed men shot dead a security guard at the Portugal embassy and escaped with 108 visa stickers, four diplomatic and 26 ordinary passports.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said cases against terrorists will be sent to special courts.
- The Pakistani cabinet will discuss on Wednesday the downsizing of government departments.
- The Afghan opposition groups have 550 Pakistani religious students in their custody.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz expects $1.5 billion loan from the IMF.
- Car smuggling is going on from Afghanistan to Pakistan through Chaman border in Baluchistan province.
